benchmark_scope.name: Kenya–Tanzania major road OSBP reference benchmark
benchmark_scope.selection_rule: Four OSBP road corridors identified by Kenyan immigration/KRA and EAC; all four also named in the replacement workbook.
benchmark_scope.denominator_note: Four named road corridors, not four exact physical gates or the complete frontier crossing population.
limits: Road class is a screening category, not measured traffic volume.
Three additional official directory entries remain background and outside the core recovery denominator.
OSM geography does not establish historical closure, legal passage or current operational status.
External published coordinates are not independent surveyed validation; datum and per-point accuracy/date are unknown.
Pair scope is selected using canonical frontier location IDs, not every possible pair of countries named in a regional event.

sources.title: One Stop Border Post (OSBP)
claims: Lists Namanga, Taveta, Lungalunga and Isebania among established Kenyan OSBPs.
sources.date_basis: Undated page; retrieval date is not an observation date.

sources.title: KRA to lead other State agencies in the launch of Namanga OSBP
claims: Identifies Namanga as a Kenya–Tanzania trade corridor and explicitly pairs Taveta/Holili, Lunga Lunga/Hororo and Isebania/Sirari.

sources.title: Gazetted Ports of Entry and Exit (PoEs) and Location
claims: Tanzania section lists seven land entries: Muhuru Bay, Isebania, Sand River Gate, Namanga, Loitoktok, Taveta and Lungalunga.
Directory labels the four OSBPs active and 24-hour, Loitoktok and Muhuru Bay active with limited hours, and Sand River closed. These are undated directory assertions, not verified current operation.
sources.date_basis: No per-entry observation or update date supplied.

sources.title: Road Transport in East Africa
claims: Names the Namanga, Sirari and Coastal corridors, connecting respectively Nairobi–Arusha, Kisii–Musoma and Mombasa–Tanga across the frontier.

sources.title: EAC Road Transport sub-sector Projects
claims: Describes the Arusha–Namanga–Athi River highway and Arusha–Holili–Taveta–Voi road connection, including their OSBPs.
sources.date_basis: Undated page with historical project milestones; not a current status check.

sources.title: One-Stop Border Post (OSBP) Status Report

sources.title: The Kenya Roads (Kenya National Highways Authority (Vesting) Order, Legal Notice 193 of 2011
sources.publisher: Kenya Law / National Council for Law Reporting
sources.date_basis: Year of legal notice; accessed edition is as at 31 December 2022. This is historical route numbering, not a current route classification claim.

These historical route references explain older OSM ref values; newer KeNHA approach designations are retained separately.

crossings.name: Loitoktok / Loitokitok
notes: Retained named land-entry reference. Not established as a major freight corridor by this bounded review; no smaller-road exception authorised.
A 2025 Danish government programme explicitly pairs Loitokitok–Tarakea. The OSM primary-road contact is near Tarakea; exact immigration facility identity remains unlocated.

crossings.name: Muhuru Bay
notes: Immigration labels this entry LAND despite its lakeshore name. Exact physical facility and road-vs-water service require review; do not silently merge road and lake transport.
